author: Owen Kane
title: Federal Way Fatal Crash: Drivers Face Homicide Charges - NewsBreak
text:
By Owen Kane ,
40 minutes ago
On Friday, October 23, at 10:45 PM, a tragic accident occurred at the intersection of South Pacific Highway and South 304th Avenue in Federal Way, Washington.
News Talk KIT
The Collision
Roberto Chris Emory (age 29) was driving a Ford F-150 with two times the legal limit of alcohol in his system,attempting to turn left at an intersection with a flashing yellow arrow. Coming the other way was 20-year-old Luis Cortes Santo, who was driving without a license and going 87 mph in a 45 mph zone.
Emory underestimated Santo’s speed and took the turn. Santos quickly swerved to avoid Emory, but the cars clipped,sending Santo’s Lexus spinning uncontrollably. The spinning Lexus went up onto the sidewalk, where it struck 16-year-old high school football player Dee-Jay Tuiasosopo. Tuiasosopo, who had just played in a game that night, flew 121 feet and died at the scene.
Photo by Martin Podsiad on Unsplash
Charges
Washington State prosecutors are charging both drivers with vehicular homicide. While Emory is blamed for driving drunk and failing to properly assess Santo’s speed, Santos is blamed for driving almost two times the speed limit.
Both men are currently locked up in the King County Jail, each held on $200,000 cash bail. Emory’s arraignment is scheduled for November 2, while Santos’s is scheduled for November 9. Vehicular Homicide is a Class A Felony in Washington State carrying a maximum sentence of life in prison along with a $50,000 fine.
The standard prison sentence for vehicular homicide while driving under the influence is roughly 7 years, while vehicular homicide for reckless driving carries a roughly 1-year prison sentence. Note that these are only for first-time offenders, and if the men have any criminal history, the sentences will drastically increase.
